decisions.reason: This reusable citrus harvesting crate is close to the firm's existing crate and agriculture-packaging know-how, so its strong relatedness makes it feasible to learn from early customer use and improve it commercially.

The foldable large container fits the firm's core reusable transport-packaging capabilities and its dedicated web presentation suggests enough early promise to justify further refinement through in-house engineering and customer feedback.
A stackable plastic crate is highly aligned with the firm's established materials, design and manufacturing knowledge, making it a natural product to retain and optimize rather than abandon early.

The medium-duty rackable pallet builds directly on the firm's pallet expertise and existing customer base, so absorptive capacity is high and the firm can credibly improve performance and market fit over time.

The spill-retention pallet extends the firm's pallet platform into a specialized use case that still relies on familiar engineering and regulatory learning, and its own-page visibility indicates meaningful strategic commitment.

This plastic pallet with load retainers leverages the firm's core pallet technology and customer problem-solving capabilities, giving management a strong basis to keep it and iterate based on operational feedback.
